items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: However Charlie Parker, of course, you know, nothing to say about Charlie, he’s – you know.

ctx.x: I know that Charlie Parker said that – Charlie Parker actually said that Willie Smith was an influence on him.

I’m sure. Well Willie was avant. I mean, he didn’t play like any other alto sax player. We had some tough alto sax players. But um, Willie was in another class. However Charlie Parker, of course, you know, nothing to say about Charlie, he’s – you know.

[laughs] I want to go back to that first assignment that – that Duke called you in ’47 and said, “I want you to arrange these two numbers, and I want them tomorrow at 2 pm,” or whenever it was. How did he get you that music? ‘Cause he’s calling you at six o’clock in the morning, and that’s giving you maybe the rest of that day and part of the next morning to get that music done.
